summary: Repeat-prompt cold-cache amplification causing intermittent P99 latency spikes and timeouts
description: Issue summary: LexiHealth reports sudden, repeatable P99 token-level latency spikes and occasional 504s when sending near-identical prompts repeatedly (chat/regen patterns). Impact: customer-facing document summarization pipeline experiences degraded throughput and intermittent timeouts during peak traffic windows (approx 15-40% of requests in a burst window). Observed behaviour: sequences of near-identical prompts that previously hit in-memory prefix/KV cache are now producing cache misses, triggering cold KV reads to the backing store which serialize and amplify latency under concurrent repeat requests. Hypothesis: a recent cache key normalization change caused semantically identical prompts to map to different prefix keys, causing cache miss amplification on repeat patterns.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use LexiHealth sample prompt set (provided in attachment) with 80% repeat-rate: send the same 6-8 token prefix followed by small completions.
2) Target 50 concurrent connections at 120 r/s for ~2 minutes.
3) Observe P50/P95/P99 for token generation and watch for 504s after ~30s.
4) Compare requests hitting cache-service (hits vs misses) and trace through request IDs collected from api-gateway logs.
Expected: high cache hit-rate for repeat-prefixes; Actual: burst of cache misses followed by P99 increases and rare 504 timeouts.

investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 2026-03-08: rollout v2026-03-08.3 deployed normalization change to cache key generator (PR #4872). No immediate alerts.
- 2026-03-10 14:00 UTC: LexiHealth reports elevated latency. Support triaged and opened this ticket.
- 2026-03-10 15:10 UTC: SRE observed cache miss-rate spike correlated with repeat-prompts.
Key findings:
- The normalization change introduced a subtle variant mapping for high-frequency punctuation and whitespace patterns in user prompts; semantically identical user inputs now sometimes map to distinct prefix keys (example: trailing non-breaking space vs normal space).
- Cache shards showed hot-cold imbalance: one shard saw a 6x increase in backend KV reads.
- Backend KV pool exhausted under concurrency causing queues and serialization of KV reads which amplified latency and produced downstream request timeouts.
- Reproduced locally by applying the same normalization rules to prompt variants; confirmed miss-rate increase and p99 amplification.
Related signals and cross-references:
- related_github_prs: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4872
- linked_issues: SUP-30012, INT-4567
- related_confluence_pages: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/KV+Cache+Design
Open hypotheses to validate:
- TTL desync between prefix cache metadata and backing store might exacerbate cold reads.
- Prefetch/backfill logic may not trigger for near-miss keys due to hash normalization mismatch.
action_taken:
Mitigations applied:
- 2026-03-10 17:45 UTC: Rolled back normalization patch (v2026-03-08.3 -> v2026-03-08.2) across us-east; immediate drop in miss-rate observed.
- Increased KV backend pool size by 30% temporarily to reduce queueing and tail latency.
- Added temporary circuit-breaker on heavy-prefix bursters to shed non-critical work.
Customer communication: LexiHealth notified of rollback and temporary mitigations; asked to validate workload during next window.
resolution: Status: Mitigated (rollback + KV pool increase). Permanent fix plan: 1) Rework normalization logic to be idempotent for common whitespace/punctuation variants and add unit tests covering edge cases; 2) Add deterministic prefix canonicalization and a graceful backfill path for near-miss keys; 3) Implement stronger shard rebalancing alerting and autoscale thresholds for KV backend; 4) Postmortem and doc update scheduled. Follow-up owner: INT ticket created (INT-4567) for permanent fix track. Estimated timeline: hotfix and tests by 2026-03-17, full rollout with monitoring by 2026-03-24.
